translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>και ανεβη ϊωαννηϲ εκ γαζαρω και απηγγιλεν ϲιμωνι τω αδελφω αυτου α ϲυνετελεϲεν δεβαιοϲ <sup>2</sup>και εκαλεϲεν ϲιμων τουϲ δυο υϊουϲ αυτου τουϲ πρεϲβυτερουϲ ιουδα και ϊωαννην κ(αι) ειπεν αυτοιϲ · εγω και οι αδελφοι μ(ου) και ο οικοϲ του πρϲ μου επολεμηϲαμεν τουϲ πολεμιουϲ ϊϲλʼ · απο νεοτητοϲ εωϲ τηϲ ϲημερον ημεραϲ και ευοδωθη εν ταιϲ χερϲιν ημω ρυϲαϲθαι τον ιϲλ πλεονακιϲ · <sup>3</sup>νυνει δε γεγηρακα και ϋμειϲ δε εν τω ελεει ϊκανοι εϲτε εν τοιϲ ετεϲιν γινεϲθε αντ εμου και του αδελφου μου και εξελθοντεϲ ϋπερ του εθνουϲ ημων η δε εκ του ουνου βοηθεια εϲτω μεθ υ̇μων <sup>4</sup>και επελεξε εκ τηϲ χωραϲ εικοϲι χιλιαδαϲ ανδρω πολεμιϲτων και ϊππειϲ και επορευθηϲαν επι τον κεδεβαιον και εκοιμηθηϲαν εν μωδιν <sup>5</sup>και αναϲταντεϲ το πρωϊ επορευθηϲαν ειϲ το πεδιον και ϊδου δυναμειϲ πολλη ειϲ ϲυναντηϲιν αυτοιϲ βαϲιλικη πεζικη και ϊππειϲ κ(αι) χιμαρρουϲ ην ανα μεϲον αυτων <sup>6</sup>και παρενεβαλε κατα προϲωπον αυτω αυτοϲ και ο λαοϲ αυτου και ιδεν τον λαον διλουμενον διαπεραϲε τον χιμαρρουν και διεπεραϲεν πρωτοϲ κ(αι) ειδον αυτον οι αδρεϲ και διεπεραϲα καθοπιϲθεν αυτω <sup>7</sup>και διειλεν τον λαον και τουϲ ιππιϲ εν μεϲω των πεζων ην δε ϊπποϲ των ϋπεναντιω πολλη ϲφοδρα <sup>8</sup>κ(αι) εϲαλπιϲαν ταιϲ ϲαλπιγξιν και ετροπωθηϲαν δαιβεοϲ κ(αι) η παρεμβολη αυτου και επεϲον εξ αυτων τραυματιαι πολλοι οι δε καταλιφθεντεϲ εφυγον ειϲ το οχυρωμα
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Then came up John from Gazera, and told Simon his father what Cendebeus had done. <sup>2</sup>Wherefore Simon called his two eldest sons, Judas and John, and said unto them, I, and my brethren, and my father’s house, have ever from my youth unto this day fought against the enemies of Israel; and things have prospered so well in our hands, that we have delivered Israel oftentimes. <sup>3</sup>But now I am old, and ye, by God’s mercy, are of a sufficient age: be ye instead of me and my brother, and go and fight for our nation, and the help from heaven be with you. <sup>4</sup>So he chose out of the country twenty thousand men of war with horsemen, who went out against Cendebeus, and rested that night at Modin. <sup>5</sup>And when as they rose in the morning, and went into the plain, behold, a mighty great host both of footmen and horsemen came against them: howbeit there was a water brook betwixt them. <sup>6</sup>So he and his people pitched over against them: and when he saw that the people were afraid to go over the water brook, he went first over himself, and then the men seeing him passed through after him. <sup>7</sup>That done, he divided his men, and set the horsemen in the midst of the footmen: for the enemies’ horsemen were very many. <sup>8</sup>Then sounded they with the holy trumpets: whereupon Cendebeus and his host were put to flight, so that many of them were slain, and the remnant gat them to the strong hold.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>τοτε ετραυματιϲθη ιουδαϲ ο αδελφοϲ ϊωαννου ϊωαννηϲ δε κατεδιωξεν αυτουϲ εωϲ ηλθεν ειϲ κεδρων ην ωκοδομηϲεν <sup>10</sup>και εφυγο ειϲ τουϲ πυργουϲ τουϲ εν τοιϲ αγροιϲ αζωτου και ενεπυριϲεν αυτην εν πυρι και επεϲο εξ αυτων ειϲ ανδραϲ διϲχιλιουϲ και απεϲτρεψεν ειϲ την ϊουδαιαν μετα ειρηνηϲ <sup>11</sup>και πτολεμαιοϲ ο του αβουβου · ην καθεϲταμενοϲ ϲτρατηγοϲ ειϲ το πεδιον ιερειχω κ(αι) εϲχεν αργυριον και χρυϲιον πολυ · <sup>12</sup>ην γαρ γαμβροϲ του αρχϊερεωϲ <sup>13</sup>κ(αι) ϋψωθη η καρδια αυτου και εβουληθη κατακρατηϲαι τηϲ χωραϲ κ(αι) εβουλευετο δολω κατα ϲιμωνοϲ και των ϋϊων αυτου αραι αυτουϲ <sup>14</sup>ϲιμων δε ην εφοδευων ταϲ πολιϲ ταϲ εν τη χωρα κ(αι) φροντιζων τα τηϲ επιμελιαϲ αυτων και κατεβη ειϲ ϊερειχω αυτοϲ και ματταθιαϲ και ιουδαϲ αδελφοϲ αυτου · ετουϲ ε ζ και ο και ρ εν μηνι αιου ουτοϲ ο μην ϲαββατʼ <sup>15</sup>και υπεδεξατο αυτουϲ ο του αβουβου · ειϲ το οχυρωματιον . ειϲ το καλουμενον δωκʼ μετα δολου ο ωκοδομηϲεν κ(αι) εποιηϲεν αυτοιϲ ποτον μεγαν και ενεκρυψεν εκει αδραϲ <sup>16</sup>και οτε εμεθυϲθη ϲιμων και οι υϊοι αυτου εξανεϲτη πτολεμαιοϲ και οι παρ αυτου κ(αι) ελαβον τα οπλα αυτων και επιϲηλθον τω ϲιμωνι ειϲ το ϲυμποϲιον κ(αι) απεκτινον αυτο και τουϲ δυο υ̇ϊουϲ αυτου και τινα τω πεδαριων αυτου
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>At that time was Judas John’s brother wounded; but John still followed after them, until he came to Cedron, which Cendebeus had built. <sup>10</sup>So they fled even unto the towers in the fields of Azotus; wherefore he burned it with fire: so that there were slain of them about two thousand men. Afterward he returned into the land of Judea in peace. <sup>11</sup>Moreover in the plain of Jericho was Ptolemeus the son of Abubus made captain, and he had abundance of silver and gold: <sup>12</sup>For he was the high priest’s son in law. <sup>13</sup>Wherefore his heart being lifted up, he thought to get the country to himself, and thereupon consulted deceitfully against Simon and his sons to destroy them. <sup>14</sup>Now Simon was visiting the cities that were in the country, and taking care for the good ordering of them; at which time he came down himself to Jericho with his sons, Mattathias and Judas, in the hundred threescore and seventeenth year, in the eleventh month, called Sabat: <sup>15</sup>Where the son of Abubus receiving them deceitfully into a little hold, called Docus, which he had built, made them a great banquet: howbeit he had hid men there. <sup>16</sup>So when Simon and his sons had drunk largely, Ptolemee and his men rose up, and took their weapons, and came upon Simon into the banqueting place, and slew him, and his two sons, and certain of his servants.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>κ(αι) εποιηϲεν αθεϲιαν μεγαλην και απεδωκεν κακα ατι αγαθων . <sup>18</sup>και εγραψεν ταυτα πτολεμαιοϲ και απεϲτιλεν ταυτα οπωϲ τω βαϲιλει δυναμιϲ ειϲ βοηθιαν και παραδω ταϲ πολειϲ αυτω και την χωραν <sup>19</sup>και απεϲτιλεν ετερουϲ ειϲ γαζαραν αραι τον ϊωαννην και τοιϲ χιλιαρχοιϲ απεϲτιλεν επιϲτολαϲ παραγενεϲθαι προϲ αυτον οπωϲ δω αυτοιϲ αργυριον και δοματα <sup>20</sup>και ετερουϲ απεϲτιλεν καταλαβεϲθαι τη ϊηλμʼ και το οροϲ του ιερου <sup>21</sup>και προδραμων τιϲ απηγγειλεν ιωαννει ειϲ γαζαρα οτι απωλετο ο πατηρ αυτου και οι αδελφοι αυτου και οτι απεϲταλκεν και ϲε αποκτιναι <sup>22</sup>και ακουϲαϲ εξεϲτη ϲφοδρα και ϲυνελαβεν τουϲ αδραϲ τουϲ ελθονταϲ απολεϲαι αυτον κ(αι) απεκτινεν αυτουϲ · επεγνω γαρ οτι εζητουν αυτον απολεϲαι <sup>23</sup>και τα λοιπα τω λογων ιωαννου και των πολεμω αυτου και των ανδραγαθιων αυτου ω ηνδραγαθηϲεν κ(αι) τηϲ οικοδομηϲ τω τιχων ων οικοδομηϲεν και των πραξεων αυτου <sup>24</sup>ιδου ταυτα γεγραπται επι βιβλιω ημερων αρχϊερωϲυνηϲ αυτου αφ ου εγενηθη αρχϊερευϲ μετα τον πρα αυτου :
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>In which doing he committed a great treachery, and recompensed evil for good. <sup>18</sup>Then Ptolemee wrote these things, and sent to the king, that he should send him an host to aid him, and he would deliver him the country and cities. <sup>19</sup>He sent others also to Gazera to kill John: and unto the tribunes he sent letters to come unto him, that he might give them silver, and gold, and rewards. <sup>20</sup>And others he sent to take Jerusalem, and the mountain of the temple. <sup>21</sup>Now one had run afore to Gazera and told John that his father and brethren were slain, and, quoth he, Ptolemee hath sent to slay thee also. <sup>22</sup>Hereof when he heard, he was sore astonished: so he laid hands on them that were come to destroy him, and slew them; for he knew that they sought to make him away. <sup>23</sup>As concerning the rest of the acts of John, and his wars, and worthy deeds which he did, and the building of the walls which he made, and his doings, <sup>24</sup>Behold, these are written in the chronicles of his priesthood, from the time he was made high priest after his father.
